simple.meaning: אָפַף (ʼâphaph) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to surround.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in 2 Samuel, Psalms, Jonah, beginning at 2 Samuel 22:5. The surrounding contexts include mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָפַף (H661) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָפַף (ʼâphaph) / H661 is traced through 2 Samuel 22:5, Psalms 18:5, Psalms 40:13, Psalms 116:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H661. aphaph אָפַף verb surround, encompass (Assyrian apâpu Zim BP 59 ) — Qal Perfect אָֽפְפוּ Psa 40:13 ; אְפָפוּנִי 18:5 +; — encompass (poetry) literal Jonah 2:6 (subject מַיִם ); figurative, subject evils & misfortunes רָעוֺת Psa 40:13 ; (followed by עָלַי ); מות מִשְׁבְּרֵי 2Sam 22:5 , compare מ ׳חֶבְלֵי Psa 18:5 , also 116:3 .

occurrences.englishText: For the waves of death surrounded me.
The cords of Sheol* Sheol is the place of the dead. were around me.
Be pleased, Yahweh, to deliver me.
The cords of death surrounded me,
I went down to the bottoms of the mountains.
